lines.text: Do you know NASA put a secret message on the parachute that landed on Mars?
This is the Perseverance rover, built from NASA's own 3D model. It landed in Jezero Crater on February eighteenth, twenty twenty-one.
It hit the Martian air at about twenty thousand kilometres an hour. Seven minutes later, it had to be standing still on the ground.
Radio signals took about eleven minutes to reach Earth. So when we heard it had hit the air, it had already landed, or crashed.
So it landed itself. It photographed the ground below, and compared it with a map it carried, to steer away from danger.
Its parachute was twenty-one metres across. And its orange and white stripes were a code.
Each stripe is a bit, a one or a zero. Each group of bits is a number, and each number is a letter of the alphabet.
The rings spell Dare Mighty Things, the motto of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. The outer ring holds its coordinates.
Space fans cracked it in a few hours.
A code in plain sight isn't private. On Orbi Transfer, an anonymous space is never listed.
To get in, you knock with its four letters. And someone inside has to let you in.
